answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Kaboom! on Nibbit, then Jumpy Dumpty on Nibbit. Fwoosh! was unplayable because the Spark bank is empty and the card is blocked by card logic. I did not play Duck and Cover because the telegraphed 12 damage is survivable at 40 HP.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing both Kaboom! cards plus Duck and Cover for 14 damage and 5 Block, but I rejected it because the enemy's 12 damage does not threaten me and the extra damage from Jumpy Dumpty is more valuable than 5 Block.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up 5 Block from Duck and Cover. It also gave up playing the second Kaboom!, but Jumpy Dumpty's 16 damage more than replaces that missing 7 damage while using the same total energy.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If the enemy intent had been a much larger attack where 5 Block could be the difference between surviving and dying, I would have considered or chosen the two Kaboom! plus Duck and Cover line. The printed 12 attack does not make that tradeoff worthwhile.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
